# Compacted Summary: Chapters 1-23 (Extended v168)

## Setting and Time
Multiple periods spanning French Revolution to 1832, continuing through evening of 24th June 1832 (rioting) and autumn Year 6. Primary locations include Paris—Rue Plumet (Valjean's house), Place de la Bastille, Prison Chargemagne, Rue des Filles-du-Calvaire No. 6 (Gillenormand residence), Champ-de-Mars, Halles district, Rue du Pont-aux-Choux, Rue de Thorigny, Marché Saint-Jean, Rue des Billettes, Rue Saint-Denis, Rue de la Chanvrerie, Rue de la Petite-Truanderie, Rue Mondétour, Pointe Saint-Eustache, Rue du Cygne, Rue des Prêcheurs. English provincial towns (Ravenmere, Elmhaven, Ostcombe, Wilwick, Salcombe, Dunstead, Staveford, Gulhaven, Kelmere, Kelford, Pontoise, Dungate). **Late night rumor/claim (winter Year 5)**: Yera Stenworth confided fire at Dunstead granary set deliberately—unverified. **Late night rumor/claim (winter Year 5)**: Fenelle Lindmere confided Stenson family once owed blood debt to Stenenridge family—unverified. **Unverified claim (mid-June 1832)**: Marald revealed Stenson family once owed blood debt to Stenenridge family. **New unverified claim (autumn Year 6)**: Stenenridge mill ledger rewritten after flood. **Kassa Brackick and Volan Stenworth married at Staveford with half parish present; couple lived in Staveford thereafter. Later, Kassa Stenson went to Dungate.** **Taric Corrley quit Staveford after quarrel, took lodgings in Dungate. Marald Corrford quit Dunstead after quarrel, took lodgings in Salcombe.** **Fenelle Lindmere followed him to Salcombe within the month.** Recent provincial observations: Ferald Stenworth complained of aching back; Thizek Stenenridge and Ferald predicted rain (wrongly); Elra Corrford laughed at story others didn't find funny; Bremira Corrford bought and regretted ribbon at stall.

## Jean Valjean and Cosette (through evening 24th June 1832)
**The wound**: Day following Jondrette visit, Valjean appeared with large inflamed wound on left arm resembling burn. Detained one month with fever; refused doctor. Cosette devoted herself to care. Recovered through March-April.

**Mysterious journeys and nocturnal manuscript**: Valjean took occasional journeys, destination unknown. Found carrying large club in garden dusk. Cosette discovered philosophical manuscript on bench—meditation on love as divine spark, recognized writer as Marius.

**Imminent departure (late June 1832)**: Morning of 24th June, Valjean told Cosette he must settle affairs; she must hold herself in readiness; linen to pack; obliged to go on journey; all to be ready in one week. **Possible destination: England.**

**Thénardier sighting and surveillance**: Caught sight of Thénardier in disguise during spring Year 6. Since that day, seen him repeatedly; certain Thénardier prowling neighborhood. Now rarely goes out with Cosette; spends time meditating on isolated slopes of Champ-de-Mars.

## Marius and Cosette's Romance (through evening 24th June 1832)
**Recognition and revelation**: Upon reading Marius's manuscript, Cosette acknowledged she had never forgotten him, had always loved him. "Fire had been smothered, and had smouldered for a time," but now "it burst forth afresh."

**Garden encounter**: Beginning autumn Year 5, Marius came every evening, entering by forcing old gate. **At height of love's voluptuousness, Marius remained absolutely chaste.** Love described as "chaste, almost shy."

**Confessions of identity (spring Year 6)**: **Cholera decimated Paris during that month.** **Marius told Cosette**: orphan, name Marius Pontmercy, lawyer, lived by writing for publishers, father was colonel and hero, on bad terms with rich grandfather, hinted at being baron. **Cosette told Marius**: brought up at Petit-Picpus convent, mother dead, father's name M. Fauchelevent, very good, gave greatly to poor.

**Marius's response and last arrangement (late June 1832)**: For last six weeks, Marius slowly taken possession of Cosette. **Upon learning of Valjean's plan to take Cosette to England in one week**: Marius declared this gravest atrocity. **Protested he has no money (owes more than ten louis to Courfeyrac), old hat, coat missing buttons, shirt ragged, elbows torn, boots leak.** **Arranged to meet in garden 26th June at nine o'clock at dusk.**

**Marius's despair (evening 24th June 1832)**: Approached grating to garden. Displaced bar and rushed headlong in. Cosette not at waiting spot. Traversed thicket, approached recess—not there. Raised eyes; shutters closed. Made tour of garden; deserted. Returned to house and knocked repeatedly, called "Cosette!" imperiously. No reply. **Fixed despairing eyes on dismal house, black and silent as tomb. Seated himself on flight of steps, heart filled with sweetness and resolution. Blessed his love, said to himself that since Cosette was gone, all that was left for him was to die.** **Marius carries loaded pistols (spring Year 6 through evening 24th June)**: Took pistols Javert gave him at time of 3d February adventure; they remained loaded.

## Father Gillenormand (evening 24th June 1832)
**Evening encounter**: Marius arrived at residence; Gillenormand grasped him at glance, found him noble and handsome. Upon learning girl's name related to Fauchelevent, declared absolutely: "Never, sir, never!"

**Sudden reversal and Marius's confession**: At tone of "never," Marius lost hope. Gillenormand seized him by collar, flung him into armchair with paternal warmth. **Marius passionately declared love for Cosette, described meeting her at Luxembourg, her father's planned departure to England, his desperation.** Stated: "She lives in a garden with an iron fence, in the Rue Plumet."

**Gillenormand's dangerous response and misrecognition**: **At words "Rue Plumet" Gillenormand interrupted his inhalation and allowed remainder of snuff to fall upon his knees.** **Delivered rambling response containing references to "Rue Blomet, Pamela, barracks, lancer," which passed before Marius like dissolving view.** **Terminated rambling in words which Marius understood as mortal insult to Cosette: "make her your mistress."** **Those words entered heart of strict young man like sword.** Octogenarian raised hands to temples with anguish, recoiled, fell back into armchair, pulseless, voiceless, tearless. **However, Marius at age when one believes nothing in line of evil. Suspicions are wrinkles; early youth has none. Gillenormand's dangerous mischaracterization left no trace in Marius's mind.**

## Café Corinthe (Halles District)
**Layout and history**: Ground floor with bar; first floor with billiard-table and wooden spiral staircase; cellar accessible via trap-door; second floor lodgings; two mansard attics under roof. Originally called _Pot-aux-Roses_; renamed _Corinthe_ after painter Natoire painted bunch of Corinth grapes on post.

**Father Hucheloup (died circa 1830)**: Possibly born chemist, was cook. Invented stuffed carps called _carpes au gras_. Amiable wine-shop-keeper with moustache; former fencing-master.

**Current proprietor and staff**: Widow Hucheloup (Mame Hucheloup) continues wine-shop. Serving-maids: Matelote (large, plump, redhaired, noisy) and Gibelotte (tall, delicate, white, lymphatic pallor, languid and weary).

**Meeting-place status**: Corinthe was meeting-place of Courfeyrac and friends. Customers drank, ate, shouted; did not pay much, always welcome.

## Laigle de Meaux and Joly (Morning 5th June 1832)
**Living arrangement**: Laigle lived more with Joly than elsewhere. Two friends ate and slept together, shared everything, called _bini_. **Morning of 5th June at Corinthe**: Joly all stuffed up with catarrh beginning to spread to Laigle. Laigle's coat threadbare; Joly well dressed.

## M. Mabeuf's Destitution and Joining Insurgents (4th June—Evening 24th June 1832)
**Character and losses**: Venerable old man of austerity and learning. **Final sacrifice (4th June 1832)**: Sold unique copy of Diogenes Laertius, returned with one hundred francs. Seated himself on overturned post in garden at dawn, motionless.

**Joining the insurgents (evening 24th June 1832)**: Encountered by band near Rue des Billettes. Set out to follow them. From that moment: uttered no word. Step suddenly became firm; artisans offered arms, refused with sign of head.

## Gavroche and the Rioting (Evening 24th June)
**Character and activities**: Street child, homeless, hungry, clever pickpocket. Armed with pistol. Evening of 24th June: arrived at Rue du Pont-aux-Choux; attempted to purchase apple-turnover but had no money; picked up fallen lancer's horse; threw stone through hair-dresser's shop panes.

**Conjunction with Enjolras's band**: Effected junction with band led by Enjolras, Courfeyrac, Combeferre, and Feuilly. Also present: Bahorel, Jean Prouvaire. Gavroche sang, whistled, hummed, ran ahead, pounded shutters with pistol butt. Completely carried away and radiant; undertaken to get everything in readiness. Filled air, everywhere at once. Enormous barricade felt him on its haunches.

**Unknown figures joining band (evening 24th June)**: **Pale, thin, small, freckled, youthful artisan in tattered blouse and patched ribbed velvet trousers emerged from lodge and spoke to Courfeyrac in voice not in least womanly.** **Near Rue des Billettes, man of lofty stature, hair turning gray, bold and daring mien joined them.** Courfeyrac, Enjolras, Combeferre remarked him but none knew him. **At work on smaller barricade, making himself useful there. Young man who had been waiting for Courfeyrac at his lodgings and inquired for M. Marius disappeared about time omnibus overturned.**

## Barricade Construction and Defense (Evening 24th June 1832)
**Two barricades constructed simultaneously**: Enjolras, Combeferre, and Courfeyrac directed everything. Both resting on Corinthe house, forming right angle. Larger shut off Rue de la Chanvrerie; other closed Rue Mondétour on side of Rue de Cygne. **Interior of barricade presented irregular square, closed on all sides, with interval of twenty paces between grand barrier and lofty houses forming background. Barricade rested on these houses, all inhabited but closed from top to bottom. An issue left free on Rue Mondétour opening through Rue des Prêcheurs into Halles, to preserve possible communication with outside.**

**Larger barricade construction**: Reached average height of six or seven feet, constructed so combatants could either disappear behind it or dominate barrier and scale crest by quadruple row of paving-stones placed on top and arranged as steps. Outside front composed of piles of paving-stones and casks bound by beams and planks entangled in wheels of Anceau's dray and overturned omnibus, had bristling inextricable aspect. Omnibus pole placed upright, held up with ropes; red flag fastened to pole floated over barricade.

**Work performed without hindrance**: All completed in less than an hour without single bear-skin cap or bayonet appearing. Terror seized whole street; shops, stables, doors, windows, blinds, skylights, shutters closed from ground floor to roof. Wine-shop alone remained open.

**Preparations for battle (evening 24th June)**: Table dragged out of wine-shop; Courfeyrac mounted on table. Enjolras brought square coffer filled with cartridges. When mob saw cartridges, tremor ran through bravest and momentary silence ensued. Posts assigned, guns loaded, sentinels stationed. Men made bullets and women lint. Large saucepan of melted brass and lead smoked over glowing brazier. Students (Combeferre, Courfeyrac, Jean Prouvaire, Feuilly, Bossuet, Joly, Bahorel, others) sought each other out and united, reciting love verses in one corner of wine-shop converted into casement. Lamp lighted in small barricade; wax torch placed in cage of paving-stones closed on three sides, all light fell on flag. Street and barricade sunk in gloom except red flag formidably illuminated.

**Waiting period**: Night fully come, nothing made appearance. Confused noises and occasional fusillades, rare, badly sustained and distant. This respite sign Government taking its time, collecting forces. These fifty men waiting for sixty thousand.

## Javert Infiltration and Discovery (Evening 24th June 1832)
**The arrest and revelation**: **Man of Rue des Billettes (previously unknown to insurgents) identified as Javert, Inspector of Police, aged fifty-two.** Had entered tap-room and seated himself at least-lighted table, holding musket between his legs. Enjolras hastily quitted Gavroche, murmured words to longshoreman who returned with three others. Four porters with broad shoulders placed themselves behind Javert's table, ready to seize him.

**Documents found on him**: Little round card pasted between two pieces of glass bearing arms of France and motto _Supervision and vigilance_; card identified him as "JAVERT, inspector of police, aged fifty-two," with signature of Prefect of Police M. Gisquet. Also had watch and purse containing several gold pieces (left undisturbed). Under watch, in fob's bottom, found paper in envelope—five lines in handwriting of Prefect of Police (content not yet revealed in text).

## Le Cabuc and Impending Violence (Evening 24th June 1832)
**Character and appearance**: **Le Cabuc, name or nickname, utter stranger to insurgents, wearing threadbare street porter's jacket.** Very drunk or assumed appearance of being so. Had seated himself with several others at table dragged outside wine-shop. While making those who vied with him drunk, examined with thoughtful air the large house at extremity of barricade, whose five stories commanded whole street and faced Rue Saint-Denis. **All at once exclaimed** (remainder of exclamation not provided in text, indicating impending violence or villainy).
